title: citrus × aurantium subf. dulcis
intro: Citrus × aurantium subf. dulcis, commonly known as bitter orange, is a plant species that belongs to the Rutaceae family and is derived from the natural hybridization of Citrus aurantium and other citrus species. It has been traditionally used in various cultures for its medicinal properties, including reducing anxiety and stress due to its sedative effects, improving digestion, and lowering blood pressure. The bioactive constituents of bitter orange, including limonoids, flavonoids, and coumarins, are responsible for its therapeutic actions, which include antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial activities. The essential oil extracted from the peel of bitter orange contains limonene, which is known for its anxiolytic, antidepressant, and antispasmodic properties.
